entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Dagobert II was the last Merovingian king of the Franks, ruling in Austrasia from 675 or 676 until his death in 679. He was the son of Chilperic II and succeeded him in the fragile Merovingian dynasty.

Dagobert II played a crucial role in the Frankish Empire's decline, as his reign marked the beginning of the end of the Merovingian period. He faced numerous challenges, including the rise of the Carolingian dynasty, which would eventually supplant the Merovingians as the dominant force in Western Europe.

Despite his relatively minor status, Dagobert II left a lasting legacy in the form of the Treaty of Verdun, which divided the Frankish Empire among his three sons, leading to the creation of the Carolingian and West Francia kingdoms.

As the Merovingian dynasty came to an end, Dagobert II's martyrdom in 679 marked the end of an era, and his legacy would be shaped by the rise of the Carolingians and the subsequent feudalization of Western Europe.

The Treaty of Verdun, which Dagobert II negotiated with his sons, remains one of the most significant documents in medieval European history, shaping the course of Western civilization for centuries to come.
